$batch_notes: Batch 3 — entries 81-130. Focus areas: (1) verb-stem compound patterns, (2) completing the 毎X system, (3) contested/shifting readings, (4) extending cross-reference chains for 手/場/間/本/生/朝/雨, (5) semantic prediction heuristics — entries chosen to test whether 'abstract+abstract=音音' etc. hold up.

characters.reading_note: 晩 has no standard kun reading. This forces 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 毎X system entry. 晩 is on-only, so this can only be 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Daily routine — '毎晩9時に寝る.'
entries.trap_note: 毎X system update: 毎日(まいにち, 音音), 毎晩(まいばん, 音音), 毎朝(まいあさ, 重箱), 毎月(まいつき/まいげつ, 重箱 or 音音), 毎年(まいとし/まいねん, 重箱 or 音音). The pattern is now clear: 毎 is always マイ(on). Classification depends entirely on whether the second character uses on or kun.

alternate_readings.context: More formal. Written/broadcast Japanese. '毎年恒例の' (annual/every year's).

characters.reading_note: In まいねん, 年=ネン is on → 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Completes the 毎X system. Dual reading with classification shift, same pattern as 毎月.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal/annual discussions — '毎年桜を見に行く' (go see cherry blossoms every year).
entries.trap_note: The 毎X system is now complete. The drill should present all five as a set and let the learner see that 毎 never changes — only the partner determines classification. Dual-reading entries (毎月, 毎年) show that the same compound can shift classification by shifting the second character's reading.

characters.reading_note: さかな → ざかな via 連濁.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: さかな → ざかな (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Completes the 焼X food trio: 焼鳥(訓訓), 焼肉(湯桶), 焼魚(訓訓). Same first element, three entries, two classifications.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurant menus, home cooking — '焼魚定食' (grilled fish set meal).
entries.trap_note: 焼X set complete: 焼鳥(やきとり, 訓訓), 焼肉(やきにく, 湯桶), 焼魚(やきざかな, 訓訓). The classification hinges on 鳥=とり(kun), 肉=にく(on), 魚=さかな(kun). The learner who sees all three together learns to check each second character independently rather than assuming a pattern from the first.

characters.reading_note: Wait — ウ is the ON reading of 雨. This makes the classification 音音, not 湯桶.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 雨 chain but with on reading ウ instead of kun あめ/あま. Shows the same character in a different reading mode.
entries.real_world_context: Weather reports — '雨量が多い' (heavy rainfall). Meteorological contexts.
entries.trap_note: 雨 chain update: 雨戸(あまど, 訓訓, あま=kun), 雨具(あまぐ, 湯桶, あま=kun), 雨量(うりょう, 音音, ウ=on). Same character, three compounds, both reading types. The partner character's formality/domain signals which: native concrete nouns (戸, 具) pull kun, Sino-Japanese technical terms (量) pull on.

characters.reading_note: ば is kun, not on. 場 on reading is ジョウ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Sixth entry in the 場=ば chain. Also corrects my own error in the analysis document — I initially second-guessed myself on this classification. 場面 is 湯桶, not 音音, because 場=ば is kun.
entries.real_world_context: Film, theater, conversation — '印象的な場面' (impressive scene). Also business — '場面に応じて' (depending on the situation).
entries.trap_note: I caught myself making the exact error this tool is designed to prevent: I temporarily thought 場面 might be 音音 because ば 'sounds' like it could be on. It's not — 場 on reading is ジョウ. This entry is calibration for the 'short common readings aren't automatically on' pattern.

characters.reading_note: Now using the on reading ジョウ, contrasting with all previous 場=ば entries.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word that provides the critical contrast: 場=ジョウ(on) here vs 場=ば(kun) in every other 場 entry so far.
entries.real_world_context: Events, facilities — '入場料' (admission fee), '入場券' (admission ticket).
entries.trap_note: 場 chain now has the key contrast: 場=ば(kun) in 立場/場所/職場/本場/役場/場面 vs 場=ジョウ(on) in 入場. The on reading appears in formal/compound Sino-Japanese contexts: 入場, 退場, 会場, 工場. The kun reading appears when 場 combines with native Japanese elements. This semantic-formality split is a genuinely predictive heuristic.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second 場=ジョウ entry. Reinforces that Sino-Japanese partner → on reading for 場.
entries.real_world_context: Events — '会場はどちらですか' (where is the venue?). Conferences, weddings, exhibitions.
entries.trap_note: 場=ジョウ cluster growing: 入場, 会場. Add 工場(こうじょう/こうば — dual reading!), 退場(たいじょう), 登場(とうじょう). The ジョウ reading is productive in formal/institutional compounds.

alternate_readings.context: Smaller-scale, workshop-like facilities. 町工場(まちこうば) = small local factory. More informal/familiar register.

characters.reading_note: In こうば reading, 場=ば is kun → still 重箱 (工=コウ is always on). But classification of こうじょう is 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading where both readings are standard but carry different nuance AND different classification. こうじょう=音音 (large factory), こうば=重箱 (small workshop).
entries.real_world_context: Industry, manufacturing, tours — '工場見学' (factory tour, always こうじょう). '町工場' (small local factory, always こうば).
entries.trap_note: This is a prize entry for the 場 chain. Same kanji pair, two readings, two classifications, and a real semantic distinction. The learner gets to see that reading choice isn't arbitrary — it encodes meaning. Large/formal = こうじょう(音音), small/familiar = こうば(重箱).

characters.reading_note: に is the 連用形 stem of にる (to simmer/boil).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the verb-stem food compound pattern. Also starts a cooking-method+物 set.
entries.real_world_context: Menu reading — 煮物 is a standard category on Japanese menus and in home cooking. '今日の煮物は何?'
entries.trap_note: Cooking-method + 物 pattern: 煮物(にもの), 焼き物(やきもの), 揚げ物(あげもの), 漬物(つけもの). All 訓訓 with verb-stem first elements. Productive, predictable, and directly relevant to menu reading.

characters.reading_note: つけ is the 連用形 stem of つける.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second in the cooking+物 set. Clean verb-stem pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, izakaya, home cooking. '漬物の盛り合わせ' (assorted pickles).

characters.reading_note: あげ is the 連用形 stem of あげる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Third in cooking+物 set. Pattern is now unmistakable.
entries.real_world_context: Menus — 揚げ物 is a standard menu category. '揚げ物は控えている' (I'm cutting back on fried food).
entries.trap_note: Note: sometimes written 揚物 without okurigana. The reading doesn't change but the visual presentation might throw off learners looking for the げ.

characters.reading_note: さし is the 連用形 stem of さす.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal food vocabulary. Verb-stem + body-part noun compound. Cross-references with 身分(みぶん, 湯桶) — same 身=み in different classification.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, supermarkets — '刺身の盛り合わせ' (assorted sashimi platter).
entries.trap_note: 身=み chain: 身分(みぶん, 湯桶), 刺身(さしみ, 訓訓). Same character, same reading, different classification based on partner.

characters.reading_note: くみ is the 連用形 stem of くむ.
たて is the 連用形 stem of たてる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Double verb-stem compound. Both elements are 連用形. Common in manufacturing/instructions.
entries.real_world_context: IKEA furniture, manufacturing — '組立説明書' (assembly instructions). '組立が簡単' (easy to assemble).
entries.trap_note: Interesting structural type: verb-stem + verb-stem. Both elements are 連用形, producing a noun. 組立, 取引(とりひき), 受付(うけつけ), 申込(もうしこみ). This is a productive compound type that's always 訓訓.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second verb+verb compound. High-frequency business vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Business — '取引先' (business partner/client), '取引条件' (terms of trade). Banking, commerce.
entries.trap_note: Note that 割引(わりびき) also contains 引=ひき→びき(連濁). Cross-reference opportunity.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Third verb+verb compound. Essential workplace vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Offices, hospitals, hotels — '受付は1階です' (reception is on the first floor). '受付時間' (reception hours). Signage everywhere.
entries.trap_note: 付=つけ(kun) here contrasts with 付=フ(on) in 貼付(ちょうふ). Same character, different reading depending on the compound's overall pattern.

characters.reading_note: もうし is the 連用形 stem of もうす.
込 is a 国字 — no on reading. Like 畑, this constrains classification.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fourth verb+verb compound. 込 being a 国字 (kun only) is a structural insight.
entries.real_world_context: Forms, applications — '申込書' (application form), '申込締切' (application deadline). Administrative situations.
entries.trap_note: 込 is a 国字 with no on reading, like 畑. Any compound with 込 has that element locked to kun. 申込, 見込み(みこみ), 追い込み(おいこみ). Structural constraint = prediction tool.

alternate_readings.context: Originally non-standard but now widely accepted. NHK permits both. Many younger speakers prefer じゅうふく.

characters.reading_note: チョウ is the prescriptive on reading here. ジュウ is increasingly accepted.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Actively contested reading. ちょうふく is prescriptive, じゅうふく is dominant in spoken Japanese. Both are 音音 but with different on readings for 重.
entries.real_world_context: Office/IT — '重複しています' (there are duplicates). Data management, form filling.
entries.trap_note: Like 施行 and 代替, this is a live reading shift. Prescriptive ちょうふく vs popular じゅうふく. Unlike those cases, both readings are 音音 — the classification doesn't change, only which on reading of 重 is used. Useful for teaching that 'which on reading?' is a real problem even when classification is clear.

alternate_readings.context: Common in spoken Japanese. Technically a misreading that has become standard through widespread use.

characters.reading_note: つづき is the 連用形 stem of つづく.
がら (pattern/nature) is a kun reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: The 'correct' reading つづきがら is 訓訓. The widespread variant ぞくがら is 重箱 (on+kun). Classification changes with reading, and the prescriptive reading is less commonly heard.
entries.real_world_context: Official forms — '続柄' (relationship to head of household). Government paperwork, insurance forms.
entries.trap_note: An honest example where the 'wrong' reading has largely won. Most people say ぞくがら. Forms still sometimes have furigana showing つづきがら. Advanced learners should know both. Good 'native speaker ≠ ground truth' entry because even the 'ground truth' here is debatable.

alternate_readings.context: Dominant in spoken Japanese. The 連濁-like voicing of ソン→ゾン is widespread.
alternate_readings.status: variant — NHK changed to permit いぞん in 2014

characters.reading_note: ソン vs ゾン is contested. NHK permitted both since 2014.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Live pronunciation shift with a specific date when NHK changed its guidance. Both readings are 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Health, psychology, tech — '依存症' (addiction), '依存関係' (dependency). Very common in modern Japanese.
entries.trap_note: NHK used to prescribe いそん exclusively. In 2014, they acknowledged いぞん as acceptable. This has a precise datestamp, making it a good concrete example for the 'readings shift over time' lesson. 存 voicing also appears in 存分(ぞんぶん) where ゾン is standard.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Formal vocabulary that appears in business documents. 漸 is unfamiliar to many learners but the on reading is regular.
entries.real_world_context: Business documents, formal writing — '漸次移行する' (transition gradually). Reports, policy documents.
entries.trap_note: Often confused with 暫時(ざんじ, temporarily) which uses different kanji. The 漸/暫 visual confusion is a separate issue but worth flagging.

characters.reading_note: あら is an older/literary kun reading form of 新. Shortened from あらた.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 新=あら is an uncommon kun form. Most learners know あたらしい and シン but not the compositional あら. Also provides contrast with 新芽(しんめ, 重箱) — same 新, different reading.
entries.real_world_context: News, mystery, military — '新手の詐欺' (a new type of scam). '新手が加わった' (fresh troops joined).
entries.trap_note: 新 reading contrast: 新芽(しんめ, 重箱 — 新=シン on) vs 新手(あらて, 訓訓 — 新=あら kun). Same character, different reading, different classification. The 'fresh/new' meaning is the same — it's the compound convention that determines on vs kun.

characters.reading_note: 連用形 of わる.
ひき → びき via 連濁.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Another verb+verb compound like 取引. Cross-references with 引=ひき/びき.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping — '割引価格' (discount price), '2割引' (20% off). Retail, travel bookings.
entries.trap_note: 引 appears in both 取引(とりひき, no 連濁) and 割引(わりびき, 連濁). Why does 連濁 apply in one but not the other? This is actually irregular — both are verb+verb compounds but 連濁 behaves inconsistently. Honest acknowledgment of where the rules get messy.

alternate_readings.context: Means 'fresh/living flowers' (as opposed to artificial). Different meaning from the art form いけばな.

characters.reading_note: いけ is from いける (to arrange/display). One of 生's many kun readings.
はな → ばな via 連濁.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 生=いけ is an unexpected kun reading. Also dual-reading with meaning split: いけばな (flower arranging art) vs せいか (fresh flowers).
entries.real_world_context: Cultural activities — '生花を習っている' (I'm learning flower arrangement). Also florist shops for せいか meaning.
entries.trap_note: 生 adds another reading to its already enormous list: 芝生(しばふ, 生=ふ), 生花(いけばな, 生=いけ). Both are unusual kun readings that only appear in specific compounds. 生 is the poster child for 'classification tells you on vs kun, but doesn't tell you WHICH kun.'

characters.reading_note: ショウ (not セイ) on reading here.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 生=ショウ (not セイ) is the tricky part. Extends the 生 cross-reference chain into on reading territory.
entries.real_world_context: Life planning, education — '生涯学習' (lifelong learning), '生涯年収' (lifetime earnings).
entries.trap_note: 生 chain growing: 芝生(ふ, kun), 生花(いけ, kun), 生涯(ショウ, on). Multiple on readings too: 生活(セイカツ) vs 生涯(ショウガイ). This character alone demonstrates why 'which reading?' is the hard problem, not 'on or kun?'

characters.reading_note: き means 'raw/undyed/natural' — specific semantic domain.
ジ is the 呉音 reading, used in 地=じ meaning 'texture/quality/ground.'

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fourth distinct 生 reading in the dataset. 生=き (raw/natural) is a specialized kun reading. 地=ジ (texture) vs チ (place) adds another layer.
entries.real_world_context: Fashion, baking, textiles — '生地がいい' (good fabric/material). 'ピザの生地' (pizza dough). Different domains, same compound.
entries.trap_note: 生 now has FOUR different readings across entries: ふ (芝生), いけ (生花), ショウ (生涯), き (生地). A fifth, なま, appears in 生ビール and is probably the most commonly known. This character is a one-kanji argument for why the tool needs more than just on/kun classification.

alternate_readings.context: Widely used in spoken Japanese. 一=ひと is kun, making this a three-character mixed compound. Many prescriptivists consider this an error.

characters.reading_note: いち is the prescriptive on reading here.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character compound with a contested reading. Demonstrates that the framework extends to longer compounds but gets messier. Also a live prescription/usage split.
entries.real_world_context: Work/projects — '仕事が一段落した' (work has reached a stopping point). Very common in business conversation.
entries.trap_note: ひとだんらく is so common that many native speakers don't know it's contested. Prescriptive いちだんらく makes it pure 音音(音). ひとだんらく would be 湯桶+音 (kun+on+on). This three-character entry tests the framework's extensibility and shows a live native-speaker error pattern.

characters.reading_note: カン here — the 'interval/between' meaning. Contrasts with 間=ま (room/space) in 客間, 手間, etc.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 間 chain with the on reading カン. Clean contrast with 間=ま entries.
entries.real_world_context: Social distancing, spacing — '間隔を空けてください' (please leave space between). Also '時間間隔' (time interval).
entries.trap_note: 間 chain: ま(kun) in 客間/手間/居間 when meaning 'room/space'; カン(on) in 間隔/時間/空間 when meaning 'interval/between.' The semantic split → reading split is one of the most reliable prediction heuristics in the dataset.

characters.reading_note: い is from いる (to be/reside).
ま = room. Same pattern as 客間, 手間.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 間=ま(room) chain. Fourth entry confirming the semantic pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Home life, real estate — '居間が広い' (the living room is spacious). Housing listings.
entries.trap_note: 間=ま (room) set now: 客間(きゃくま, 重箱), 手間(てま, 訓訓), 居間(いま, 訓訓). The ま reading is stable across all when the meaning is 'room.' Compare 間隔(かんかく, 音音) where the meaning is 'interval' and the reading shifts to カン.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends both the 本=ホン chain (本棚, 本場) and the 物=もの chain (物語, 煮物, 漬物).
entries.real_world_context: Shopping, art, food — '本物のダイヤモンド' (real diamond). '本物の味' (authentic flavor). Antique/art authentication.
entries.trap_note: 本=ホン now appears in 本棚(重箱), 本場(重箱), 本物(重箱) — consistently 重箱 when paired with a native kun-reading noun. Also 手本(てほん, 湯桶), 見本(みほん, 湯桶), 絵本(えほん, 湯桶) — consistently 湯桶 when 本 is the second element with on reading ホン. The character's position in the compound predicts the classification pattern.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 手=て chain into more business vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Business, logistics, police — '手配する' (arrange/prepare), '指名手配' (wanted person). Travel planning, event management.
entries.trap_note: 手=て chain now: 手紙(訓訓), 手間(訓訓), 手本(湯桶), 手帳(湯桶), 手数(湯桶), 手配(湯桶). Pattern visible: 手+kun-noun = 訓訓, 手+on-noun = 湯桶. Perfectly predictable.

characters.reading_note: シュ on reading — contrasts with every other 手 entry in the dataset.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Critical contrast entry. Every other 手 entry uses て(kun). This one uses シュ(on). Same character, finally in a different reading mode.
entries.real_world_context: Discussion, debate — '手段を選ばない' (will stop at nothing). Business strategy, ethics discussions.
entries.trap_note: 手 chain culmination: 手紙(て, 訓訓), 手間(て, 訓訓), 手本(て, 湯桶), 手帳(て, 湯桶), 手数(て, 湯桶), 手配(て, 湯桶), 手段(シュ, 音音). Six entries as て(kun), one as シュ(on). The on reading appears when the partner is also on (段=ダン). The formality heuristic applies: 手段 is more abstract/formal than 手紙 or 手帳.

characters.reading_note: チ here (not ジ). Contrasts with 生地(きじ) where 地=ジ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common address vocabulary. 地=チ vs ジ is a useful disambiguation: チ for 'ground/land' (番地, 土地, 地方), ジ for 'texture/quality/ground-base' (生地, 地元... wait, 地元=じもと uses ジ but means 'local'). The split isn't perfectly semantic.
entries.real_world_context: Addresses — '番地を教えてください.' Mail, registration, navigation.
entries.trap_note: 地 has two on readings: チ and ジ. Some patterns: 地震(じしん), 地元(じもと), 生地(きじ) use ジ. 番地(ばんち), 土地(とち), 地方(ちほう) use チ. The split is partly semantic, partly fossilized. Not perfectly predictable but worth noting.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 朝 chain. Colloquial/casual register. Both characters kun = 訓訓.
entries.real_world_context: Casual conversation — '朝飯前' (easy/before breakfast). 'まだ朝飯食べてない' (haven't eaten breakfast yet).
entries.trap_note: 朝 chain: 朝刊(チョウカン, 音音), 毎朝(まいあさ — 朝=あさ, 重箱), 朝日(あさひ, 訓訓), 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓). When 朝 means 'morning' in casual/native contexts → あさ(kun). When it appears in formal/Sino-Japanese compounds → チョウ(on). 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音) vs 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓) — same meaning, different register, different classification.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Register pair with 朝飯. Hotel/formal contexts use ちょうしょく. Casual contexts use あさめし/あさごはん.
entries.real_world_context: Hotels — '朝食は何時からですか' (what time does breakfast start?). Formal dining situations.
entries.trap_note: 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音, formal) vs 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓, casual). The register-classification correlation is strong: formal Sino-Japanese → 音音, casual native Japanese → 訓訓. This pair makes the pattern explicit.

characters.reading_note: ゆう is KUN. Despite the formal compound, 夕 uses its kun reading. This makes the compound 湯桶, not 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Breaks the register-classification pattern. 夕食 LOOKS like it should be 音音 (parallel to 朝食) but isn't because 夕=ゆう is kun. The formality heuristic fails here.
entries.real_world_context: Hotels, restaurants — '夕食は7時からです.' Same register as 朝食 but different classification.
entries.trap_note: This is a critical heuristic-breaker. 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音) and 夕食(ゆうしょく, 湯桶) are used in identical contexts and feel equally formal, but have different classifications because 朝=チョウ(on) while 夕=ゆう(kun). The learner who assumes 'formal = 音音' gets burned here. Classification requires checking each character, not guessing from register.

characters.reading_note: kun, same as in 夕食 and 夕刊.
ハン(on) here, unlike 朝飯 where 飯=めし(kun).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Interesting: 夕飯 is less formal than 夕食 but 飯 uses its ON reading ハン, not kun めし. Register doesn't predict reading here either.
entries.real_world_context: Home/casual — '夕飯何にする?' (what shall we have for dinner?). Family conversation.
entries.trap_note: Meal compound matrix is now rich: 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音), 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓), 夕食(ゆうしょく, 湯桶), 夕飯(ゆうはん, 湯桶). 夕 is always ゆう(kun). But 飯 shifts: めし(kun) in casual 朝飯, ハン(on) in 夕飯 even though 夕飯 is also casual. The register-reading correlation is weaker than it first appears.

characters.reading_note: し is not a standard reading of 時.
ぐれ is not a standard reading of 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Nature/weather 熟字訓. Extends the cluster: 梅雨, 雪崩, 時雨.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — late autumn/early winter intermittent rain. Literary/poetic. Also food: 牛肉時雨煮(ぎゅうにくしぐれに) — a dish name.
entries.trap_note: Also extends the 雨 chain — 雨 has now appeared as あめ, あま, ウ, and ぐれ(熟字訓). Four different surface forms for one character.

characters.reading_note: さ derives from さつき (旧暦五月). Not a standard reading of 五.
み is not a standard reading of 月.
だれ is not a standard reading of 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character 熟字訓. Literary/seasonal vocabulary. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Literary, seasonal — rainy season rain (originally lunar calendar fifth month). Also business jargon: '五月雨式に' (in a trickle/piecemeal). '五月雨式の報告' (reports coming in dribs and drabs).
entries.trap_note: The business usage 五月雨式 is surprisingly common — it's how people describe things arriving irregularly over time. An advanced learner working in a Japanese office will encounter this metaphorical use. The literal weather meaning is literary/poetic.

alternate_readings.context: Means 'one day' (duration). Different meaning from ついたち (first day of the month).
Business/formal — '一日付で' (effective the first of the month). Written formal contexts.

characters.reading_note: つい is not a standard reading of 一.
たち is not a standard reading of 日.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three readings, two meanings, two classifications. Extends the calendar 熟字訓 domain (alongside 昨日/今日/明日).
entries.real_world_context: Calendar — '一日に会議があります' (there's a meeting on the first). Also '一日中' (all day long) uses いちにち. Context determines reading.
entries.trap_note: 一日 is a masterclass in dual-reading complexity: ついたち (first of month, 熟字訓), いちにち (one day, 音音), いっぴ (first of month, formal, 音音). The meaning determines the reading. Calendar dates are a whole sub-system of irregular readings that could be its own module.

alternate_readings.context: Straightforward on-on reading. Used in formal/clinical contexts. '二十歳以上' in legal text could be either reading.

characters.reading_note: は is not a standard reading of 二.
た is not a standard reading of 十.
ち is not a standard reading of 歳.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character 熟字訓. Culturally important — coming of age. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Coming-of-age day, legal age, social situations — 'はたちになったら' (when you turn twenty). Celebrations, life milestones.
entries.trap_note: はたち derives from the old Japanese counting system (はた=20). This archaic number reading only survives in this word. Like ついたち, it's a calendar/number 熟字訓 — a domain where undecomposable readings cluster thickly.

characters.reading_note: コン is the 呉音. Most learners know only ケン.
リュウ is the 呉音. Most learners know only リツ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters use 呉音 readings. Buddhist/temple vocabulary. Same pattern as 境内 — 呉音 signals religious domain.
entries.real_world_context: Temple visits — 'この寺は800年前に建立された' (this temple was built 800 years ago). Sightseeing, history.
entries.trap_note: 建立 and 境内 both use 呉音 readings, and both are temple/religious vocabulary. This is a genuine pattern: Buddhist terminology often preserves 呉音 readings. If a learner encounters an unfamiliar compound in a temple context, trying 呉音 is a viable strategy.

characters.reading_note: こころ → ごころ via 連濁.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: こころ → ごころ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 物=もの chain. The 連濁 on こころ is an important pattern — it appears in 親心(おやごころ), 乙女心(おとめごころ), etc.
entries.real_world_context: Childhood memories — '物心がついた頃' (from the time I became aware/conscious). Memoir-style conversation.
entries.trap_note: 心=ごころ(連濁) is a productive pattern in X+心 compounds: 物心, 親心(おやごころ), 乙女心(おとめごころ). When 心 is the second element after a kun-reading noun, expect ごころ.

characters.reading_note: ブツ → ぶっ via 促音 before シ.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ブツ → ぶっ (促音 before シ).
entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Provides the 物=ブツ(on) contrast with 物=もの(kun) entries. Also 促音 pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Science, health — '物質の性質' (properties of a substance). '危険物質' (hazardous substance).
entries.trap_note: 物 chain: もの(kun) in 物語/煮物/本物/物心 vs ブツ(on) in 物質/物理(ぶつり)/人物(じんぶつ). Same formality split: concrete/everyday → もの, abstract/scientific → ブツ.

characters.reading_note: ね is the 連用形 stem of ねる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character compound: kun+kun+on. Doesn't fit neatly into the four categories. Demonstrates the framework's limit with longer compounds.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '朝寝坊した!' (I overslept!). Casual conversation.
entries.trap_note: Three-character compounds require recursive classification: 朝寝(あさね, 訓訓) + 坊(ボウ, on). The overall compound is kun+kun+on, which has no clean label in the four-category system. This reinforces the recommendation to focus the drill on two-character compounds.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Anchor for the abstract+abstract → 音音 heuristic. Two abstract Sino-Japanese concepts = on+on.
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '練習する' (to practice). Sports, music, language learning.
entries.trap_note: Included primarily to build the heuristic testing set. 練(refine) + 習(learn) = two abstract verbs of Chinese origin → 音音. Predicted by the semantic heuristic. Building enough anchor examples makes the heuristic testable.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Another abstract+abstract → 音音 anchor.
entries.real_world_context: Professional situations — '経験がある' (have experience). Résumés, interviews, business discussion.
